Review: An Astronaut's Guide to Life on Earth

by Jeff Foust

Monday, November 18, 2013 Bookmark and Share
An Astronaut’s Guide to Life on Earth: What Going to Space Taught Me About Ingenuity, Determination, and Being Prepared for Anything by Chris Hadfield Little, Brown and Company, 2013 hardcover, 304 pp., illus. ISBN 978-0-316-25301-7 US$28.00
One year ago, few people outside of Canada who didn’t follow spaceflight knew of Canadian astronaut Chris Hadfield.

...

During his five months in space, Hadfield hadn’t heroically saved the station, or the Earth, or made some kind of major discovery or breakthrough.
* However, while the concept of writing a book may be rather old-school, An Astronaut’s Guide to Life on Earth is not the typical astronaut memoir.
Instead, Hadfield harnessed the growing power of social media to reach out directly to the public. He posted images of the Earth he took while on the station to his Twitter account and videos of life

...

Hadfield does tell a lot about his life, including his path to becoming an astronaut and his three space flights, in the book, but the book is not structured as a basic, chronological biography. Instead, as the title suggests, Hadfield offers advice in the form of the lessons he learned on his path to becoming an astronaut that he argues apply to those who have no desire to be astronauts.
